description: Porphyry copper-molybdenum-gold: stockwork and disseminated ore in zoned alteration shells around oxidised arc porphyry stocks at convergent margins.

source.note: ore_genesis_modeling.md Q7 example (illustrative shape): arc magma pulses
Q7 example; hot, hydrous, oxidised magmas (Richards 2003)

driver.note: peak near 15° (Butterworth et al. 2016); tails are design
25–70 Myr slab age (Butterworth et al. 2016); tails are design

pathway.note: Q7 example; crustal stress controls ascent (Richards 2003)

trap.note: Q7 example; thickened compressive arcs (Cooke et al. 2005)

notes: RICHNESS (owner, decisions log 2026-10-02, "Rich Deposits, Thinner Scatter, Also make deposits use some of the vanilla ore vein features"): the zone densities were raised and the richest zone carries raw-ore blocks (raw_share: that share of its ore blocks is the raw-ore block, as vanilla's ore veins carry 2 %); game-choice, ledger ORE-266; the richness settings scale both in the world (ORE-262). Measured in docs/science/deposits.md.

Sizing: USGS OFR 2008-1155 (Singer, Berger & Moring 2008), Table 1 (PDF p. 9): all porphyry Cu deposits, n = 422; by-product percentiles count unreported grades as zero; presence = n_reported / 422 from the report's data file PorCuTX2008.txt; correlations (Pearson r of log10) from the text, PDF p. 8. See crates/deeptime-core/data/usgs/porphyry_cu.json.
Deposit density 4 / 15 / 35 per 100,000 km² and the 2 km same-deposit rule: Singer, Berger & Menzie 2005 (USGS authors; Pubs Warehouse record 70197200) and OFR 2008-1155 PDF p. 4.
PLACEHOLDER: ore_density_t_m3 2.7 (no USGS value found; generic intermediate-felsic intrusive rock).

Geometry: aspect from SIR 2010-5070-B (median ore area 0.6 km², Table E1 p. 28; hypogene ore generally 1–1.5 km tall, p. 25); formation depth 1.5 km = median emplacement depth of the Cu subtype (OFR 2008-1155 Fig. 24, digitised).
Design values: curves' tails, tract_threshold, clustering radii, zoning fractions and densities, lithocap and gossan sizes, size_mult_h 12 (a median porphyry ≈ 20 blocks across).
Create stones (decisions file): serpentinite (veridium) is a preferred copper host at weight 1.5; the gossan is ironstone (ochrum → gold) and carries gold.

Density basis measured (decisions log 2026-09-29, "Use the USGS mean density"): Singer, Berger, Menzie & Berger 2005 give the distribution over 19 well-explored control areas, so the survivor formula takes its mean, 17.8 per 100,000 km² (the split lognormal through 4 / 15 / 35), the expectation over many tracts. Only survivors whose top lies within 1 km of the surface count toward it (Circular 1178 printed p. 5: USGS assessments count deposits to 1 km; a deposit counts if any part is within 1 km); deeper survivors are sites on top. Counts (survivor formula, decisions log 2026-09-29, plan §8.6 as built): the density counts deposits that survive to the present, as USGS does; the engine forms more (deposits/survival.rs) so that the expected survivors are ρ · permissive area · count_mult (ρ the mean 17.8, above). balance.count_mult stays 1: a pack lever, not a calibration. On the six 500-Myr pipeline_quick_16k test landscapes the permissive arcs cover 40,000–82,000 km², so 6–12 survivors are expected; a third to a half of the porphyries formed survive (STATUS.md, 2026-09-29 survivor formula).
